caption:
We built a free Schengen 90/180 calculator because people keep counting it wrong.

The rule is a rolling window, not a calendar year. Take your entry date, count back 180 days, add every Schengen day inside it. Under 90 and you are clear.

Most people count from January. That is not how it works — and since the EU began recording crossings digitally, a miscount is a logged overstay rather than a quiet mistake.

The calculator is free on our site. No signup.

slides.headline: MOST PEOPLE COUNT THEIR 90 DAYS WRONG.
slides.sub: So we built something that does it for you.
slides.note: The 90/180 rule is a rolling window. It moves with you, daily. It never resets in January.

slides.answer: IT IS NOT A CALENDAR YEAR.
slides.body: In any 180 days counting backwards from your entry date, your total days inside Schengen must stay under 90.
slides.note: The window moves every single day. Yesterday's answer is not today's answer.

slides.headline: TO COUNT IT YOURSELF
items: Add every day spent inside Schengen in that window
Under 90 and you are clear to enter

slides.headline: YOUR DAYS ARE COUNTED AUTOMATICALLY NOW
slides.body: The EU's Entry/Exit System records short-stay crossings digitally instead of stamping passports. Miscounting is no longer invisible.
slides.takeaway: An overstay you did not intend still reads as an overstay.
